_purpose: Meta descriptions for guides whose summary falls outside 110-160 characters. The guide records in data/authority/content_registry.json are hash-frozen, so the search-result text lives here instead; lib/seo.ts guideMetaDescription() reads this first, then the summary when it already fits. scripts/validators/validate_rendered_seo_contract.mjs fails the build on any rendered description outside 110-160.

descriptions.1-month-wedding-checklist: One month out, stop designing and start verifying: reconcile contracts, final guest and meal counts, seating, balances, transport, and role timelines.
descriptions.12-month-wedding-checklist: A 12-month wedding plan by quarter: secure the venue and scarce vendors first, build guest and design systems mid-year, then reconcile at the end.
descriptions.18-month-wedding-checklist: With 18 months, compare venues and priority vendors without manufacturing urgency, then book the scarce ones and schedule design and guest work later.
descriptions.3-month-wedding-checklist: A three-month wedding checklist is a critical path: secure the legal, venue, vendor, guest, and payment essentials, then cut anything that is decoration.
descriptions.accessible-wedding-planning-checklist: Plan accessibility early: routes, seating, sightlines, sound, and dietary needs constrain venue and layout decisions that lock long before the day.
descriptions.backyard-wedding-checklist: A backyard wedding is a temporary event site: plan power, restrooms, parking, weather shelter, permits, insurance, and cleanup before any decor.
descriptions.bridal-shower-checklist: A bridal shower is somebody else's hosted event, so settle who decides and who pays first, then the guest list, the date, and the party itself.
descriptions.day-of-coordinator-checklist: A day-of coordinator can only run what they were handed: the timeline, vendor sheet, contracts, payments, and a list of decisions they may make alone.
descriptions.elopement-planning-checklist: An elopement drops guests but not legal rules: check the licence, waiting period, witnesses, officiant authority, and location permits before travel.
descriptions.post-wedding-return-checklist: Close out the wedding: return rentals and borrowed items, settle vendor balances and gratuities, secure gifts and documents, and log any damages.
descriptions.wedding-attire-lead-time-checklist: Wedding attire runs on suppliers' calendars: get order and alteration lead times in writing, then time the final fitting so the fit still holds.
descriptions.wedding-emergency-kit: Pack a wedding emergency kit by failure mode (garment, body, paper, power, weather) in two bags, one for getting ready and one for the venue.
descriptions.wedding-planning-binder: Set up a wedding planning binder that separates live decisions from inspiration, with a tab for every contract, payment, guest record, and handoff.
descriptions.wedding-vendor-list: Build a wedding vendor list with category, status, contact, scope, contract, payment dates, and handoff owner, then turn it into a day-of directory.
descriptions.wedding-venue-selection-checklist: Choose a wedding venue by its constraints before its look: seated capacity, access, curfew, vendor rules, and what the weather fallback holds.
descriptions.wedding-budget-20000: A $20,000 wedding budget can buy more vendor depth but still needs category caps, taxes and service charges modeled, and month-by-month cash tracking.
descriptions.wedding-budget-contingency: Wedding contingency is reserved money for approved unknowns: pick the reserve, keep it separate, decide who approves draws, and log every one.
descriptions.wedding-budget-for-50-guests: Build a 50-guest wedding budget from your total ceiling and top priorities, split fixed from per-guest costs, and quote venue and food for 50.
descriptions.wedding-budget-template: A wedding budget template needs six columns per line: estimate, quote, contracted, paid, balance, and the month the balance falls due.
descriptions.wedding-hidden-costs-checklist: Hidden wedding costs are contract terms nobody modeled: taxes, service charges, gratuities, delivery, overtime, permits, insurance, and returns.
descriptions.wedding-monthly-cash-flow: Plan wedding cash flow month by month: map every deposit and balance to its due date, add contributor timing, and find peak months before they hit.
descriptions.wedding-vendor-payment-tracker: Track every wedding vendor payment: contract total, deposit, installments, balance, due dates, payer, method, and a receipt for each one.
descriptions.wedding-day-logistics-timeline: Wedding day logistics fail at handoffs: anchor the fixed times, work back through travel, load-in, and setup, and name an owner for each handoff.
descriptions.wedding-day-timeline-template: A wedding day timeline template where every row has a duration, an owner, and a location, so it can be cut into versions for each vendor and role.
descriptions.wedding-music-cue-sheet: A wedding music cue sheet lists every cue in order with start and stop points, one owner each, the venue's real sound equipment, and offline copies.
descriptions.wedding-party-timeline: Give the wedding party a role-specific timeline: arrival and ready times, attire, transport, photos, ceremony staging, and reception duties.
descriptions.wedding-reception-flow-timeline: Sequence a wedding reception so speeches never collide with a course: arrival, seating, service, toasts, and dancing checked against the kitchen.
descriptions.wedding-rehearsal-timeline: Run a wedding rehearsal in under an hour: processional in reverse, positions before movement, the full sequence twice, then readings and handoffs.
descriptions.alphabetical-vs-table-order-seating-char: Alphabetical seating charts help guests find their names; table-order charts help staff see each table. Keep both from one guest list.
descriptions.sweetheart-table-vs-head-table: Sweetheart table or head table? Compare floor space, who gets separated from partners, sightlines, service, speeches, and how you want dinner to feel.
descriptions.wedding-escort-card-data-export: Generate escort-card data from the final seating plan, not from memory: freeze names, table labels, households, and meal markers, then proofread.
descriptions.wedding-guest-list-headcount-control: Treat the guest list as a capacity decision: fix the venue ceiling, list by household with priority tiers, and release held seats only after declines.
descriptions.wedding-meal-count-dietary-tracking: Keep meal choice, allergies, and dietary needs on each guest's row, reconcile them against RSVPs, and send the caterer one dated breakdown per change.
descriptions.wedding-rsvp-tracking-system: RSVP tracking breaks at the household: invites go to households but meals and seats are per person, so keep one row per guest and reconcile totals.
descriptions.wedding-seating-chart-for-150-guests: Seating 150 wedding guests is a data problem: table and guest IDs, household groups, capacity checks, meal and access fields, and change control.
descriptions.wedding-seating-chart-for-50-guests: Fifty wedding guests usually fit five to seven tables. Choose the layout from venue-approved table sizes, service space, households, and access.
descriptions.wedding-seating-chart-meal-tracker: Track meal choices on the seating chart per guest, separate child and vendor meals, flag unknowns, and count by table to match the caterer's list.
descriptions.wedding-seating-chart-vendor-handoff: Hand vendors a dated master seating plan with only the fields each one needs: counts, alphabetical and table views, meals, and a corrections contact.
